summary: Discovery focused on model selection for multilingual summarization and tool-calling workflows. Customer evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and latency; needs 32k+ context for long-form documents, multilingual support (ES/JP), and function/tool-calling for retrieval and connector calls. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, run latency estimates for 32k/64k configs, schedule POC scoping session.
topics: open-model comparisons (Llama variants, Mistral, Redwoods curated models)
tool-calling / function calling and retrieval integration
hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ethan from Redwood, this is Priya on the engineering side. Um quick agenda — model selection, context length, multilingual, and then deployment options, and security.
[00:22] Lena Torres: Hi thanks, yeah big ones for us: we process multi-page legal and clinical documents, so context is huge - we need 30k to 60k depending on use case. Also, must support Spanish and Japanese equally.
[00:35] Priya Rao: Got it. From a model perspective we usually look across a couple families — open Llama2-ish weights, Mistral-like, and Redwood-curated variants. For 32k and up we typically recommend models that have native long-context or we use our context-window extension with KV caching.
[01:10] Ravi Gupta: Quick q — what does "KV cache" mean in practice? we've tried it on our self-hosted stack and saw memory blow up.
[01:25] Priya Rao: Yeah so KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K V cache) is per-request key/value memory for attention. Redwood's runtime manages KV eviction and prefix caching to avoid re-sending unchanged history. For long docs we do chunking + prefix cache so you don't keep the whole doc in GPU RAM simultaneously, which reduces memory spikes.
[01:55] Hannah Lee: And tool-calling — we need to call our internal retrieval API and a billing/ERP connector. Does Redwood support function calling like OpenAI's approach?
[02:10] Ethan Chen: Yes — hosted API supports function/tool calling, structured outputs; SE will show how we wire retrieval + function calls. For Private you can run the same control plane with connectors inside your VPC.
[02:40] Marco Diaz: Security question: we have strict residency and KMS requirements for keys — any SOC2/ISO stuff?
[02:55] Priya Rao: We have SOC 2 attestations for Hosted and Dedicated control planes; Private deployments can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. I'll share the security brief — it includes SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit log examples.
[03:20] Lena Torres: On model quality — we're sensitive to hallucinations in clinical text. Are there recommended models that are better for factuality?
[03:35] Priya Rao: For factuality we often start with models finetuned on instruction-following and medically-oriented corpora. Open Llama-extended variants perform decently; Redwood also has verification profiles and you can pin a model version. We also recommend prompt engineering + retrieval augmented generation to reduce hallucination.
[04:10] Ravi Gupta: Cost/latency tradeoffs — what's realistic for 32k context? We need sub-1s token latency for interactive parts but batching helps for throughput — can Dedicated hit that?
[04:30] Priya Rao: Sub-1s for token generation with 32k is hard if you're running the biggest 70b models in FP16; latency depends on sequence length and hardware. Dedicated on A100/A10Gs with optimized kernels and model sharding can get you low passed token latency for shorter prefixes; for long initial prompts the first token can be heavier. We can do a benchmark: our suggestion is POC on Dedicated with a few representative prompt sets.
[05:05] Ethan Chen: For POC we usually recommend hosted to validate quality quickly, then Dedicated for production throughput and data isolation, and Private if you need full network isolation or on-prem.
[05:30] Hannah Lee: Are there specific open models you recommend for Spanish/Japanese? We've seen Llama2 decline on Japanese sometimes.
[05:45] Priya Rao: For multilingual smaller models, models trained on multilingual data — there are Mistral-family and some community Japanese-specialized checkpoints. Redwood-curated catalog flags models with better multilingual benchmarks. We can run our eval harness against your sample prompts in ES/JP.
[06:12] Ravi Gupta: What's the operational difference between Dedicated and Private? Our infra team wants to know about upgrades and rollback.
[06:28] Priya Rao: Dedicated is a Redwood-managed GPU pool in a customer tenant with reserved capacity, we handle kernel updates, autoscaling within reserved limits, and SLAs. Private is customer-controlled network and optionally on-prem; upgrades are coordinated — you get more control but also more planning for rollouts.
[07:05] Lena Torres: Any limits on context length per model? Like can we do 128k?
[07:20] Priya Rao: Some models have native 128k variants but they trade off with parameter size and throughput. Practically we see stable results up to 64k for production; 128k is possible but needs special attention to memory and may require model quantization and sharding. We'll run the memory/latency estimates for your doc sizes.
[07:55] Marco Diaz: We use AES-GCM with customer KMS; how would keys be managed for Hosted?
[08:10] Ethan Chen: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. For strict KMS policies Private + KMS integration is typical.
[08:35] Hannah Lee: On pricing — is there a per-token plus reserved capacity model?
[08:45] Ethan Chen: Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding; Dedicated is capacity-based with monthly commit + lower per-unit costs; Private is enterprise licensing. We'll send a pricing outline.
[09:05] Ravi Gupta: For the model selection experiment, we want to compare Llama2-Chat-70B (quantized), a Mistral-large 30B, and Redwood-curated 32k variant — can Redwood run those comparisons?
[09:25] Priya Rao: Yes — bring sample prompts and we will run accuracy, latency, and token-cost comparisons and return a spreadsheet. Ethan will share the benchmark template now.
[09:45] Ethan Chen: (shares link) model-benchmarks.xlsx — contains tabs for prompts, eval metrics, latency, and cost.
[10:05] Lena Torres: Our timeline is tight: POC in 3 weeks, production in Q3 if POC looks good. Decision factors: cost per inference, latency SLOs, data residency.
[10:30] Priya Rao: That's doable. For a 3-week POC we recommend: hosted eval for quality (week 1), Dedicated latency/cost benchmark (week 2), and POC scoping + security review (week 3).
[11:00] Ravi Gupta: Do you support on-demand tool execution? we want to call retrieval and then run a deterministic summarizer in our infra.
[11:20] Priya Rao: Yes tool-calling supports structured outputs; you can have the model return JSON with function name and args and Redwood will surface that. For critical determinism you can separate the summarizer into a deterministic post-processor.
[11:55] Hannah Lee: Any gotchas with quantized models and multilingual? we saw quality drop in JP with int8.
[12:10] Priya Rao: Quantization can affect tokenization and subtle distributional shifts — we recommend running QA across languages; in some cases mixed precision or selective quantization gives a better balance.
[12:40] Lena Torres: Ok can you also include model explainability / evals like rouge/bertscore?
[12:55] Priya Rao: Absolutely — we'll run rouge, bertscore, and custom hallucination checks with your reference outputs.
[13:20] Ethan Chen: quick check on stakeholders — who from your side will sign off on security?
[13:35] Lena Torres: That's me for technical signoff and our compliance officer will need to review. I'll loop them in after this.
[13:50] Marco Diaz: For Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[14:05] Ethan Chen: Depends on region and GPU type — typical min is 4xA100 or equivalent for enterprise reserved pools; we'll include an estimate.
[14:30] Ravi Gupta: Can you simulate worst-case throughput? our peak batch jobs process 200 requests/min with long context.
[14:45] Priya Rao: Yes we'll do throughput testing and show autoscaling/burst behavior and cost implications.
[15:10] Hannah Lee: Any other enterprise features like audit logs per request?
[15:25] Priya Rao: Yes per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.
[15:50] Ethan Chen: All right let's capture next steps — we'll run the three-model benchmark, provide latency/cost estimates for 32k/64k contexts, and share the security brief.
[16:05] Lena Torres: Great — expecting the benchmark spreadsheet and security doc. Also pricing.
[16:20] Ethan Chen: We'll aim to get initial results back in a week for quality, then Dedicated latency tests the following week.
[16:40] Hannah Lee: Sounds good, thanks.
[16:50] Ethan Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for POC scoping and send the artifacts.
[17:05] (call ends)
Note: transcription contains minor mis-recognitions (e.g., "K V cache", "Redwood dedicate") and occasional run-on sentences typical of call transcripts.
